zero_omission_notes.summary: This chapter explores line relationships in a plane: intersecting lines, points of intersection, vertically opposite angles, linear pairs, perpendicular lines, and parallel lines. It uses paper folding and geometric deduction to prove angle equality and parallel line properties.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Two non-coincident lines intersect at at most one point. Four angles are formed. 1. Vertically Opposite Angles are equal: a = c, b = d. 2. Linear Pairs sum to 180°: a + b = 180°, b + c = 180°.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Intersection Uniqueness
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Two straight lines can never intersect at two distinct points.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Parallel lines never meet regardless of extension, maintaining constant perpendicular distance. Perpendicular lines intersect at 90°.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Grid Parallelism
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Identify parallel lines on dot grid paper.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Folding paper in half creates parallel line creases. Folding perpendicularly creates right angles.

practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.aim_or_objective: Construct parallel and perpendicular creases using paper folding
procedure_or_steps: Fold vertically in half across horizontal creases.
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.observations_or_results: Horizontal creases are parallel to each other. Vertical crease is perpendicular to all horizontal creases.
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.conclusion_or_principle: Sequential parallel folds create parallel lines; orthogonal folds produce perpendicular lines.

textbook_exercises.question: Can two straight lines intersect at more than one point?
textbook_exercises.answer: No. Two distinct straight lines can intersect at most at one unique point.

objective_questions_1_mark.question: If two lines intersect and one angle is 45°, what is its vertically opposite angle?

short_answer_questions.question: Two intersecting lines form a linear pair x and y. If x = 2y, find x and y.

analytical_reasoning_questions.question: Two lines intersect forming angles a, b, c, d in clockwise order. If a = 35°, find b, c, d.
analytical_reasoning_questions.answer:
1. b = 180° - 35° = 145° (Linear pair).
2. c = a = 35° (Vertically opposite).
3. d = b = 145° (Vertically opposite).

comprehensive_long_answers.question: Explain the geometric properties of vertically opposite angles and linear pairs with proofs.
comprehensive_long_answers.answer:
1. Linear Pair Postulate: Adjacent angles on a straight line sum to 180°. Hence a + b = 180° and b + c = 180°.
2. Proof of Vertically Opposite Angles: Since a + b = 180° and b + c = 180°, we have a + b = b + c. Subtracting b from both sides yields a = c.

common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.common_error_or_misconception: Assuming line segments are parallel just because they do not meet within a small drawing area.
common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.correct_fact_or_method: Line segments must remain equidistant when extended indefinitely to be parallel.
